# dsh-remote-editor
A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web plugin that opens the current session's workspace in **Cursor, VS Code,
VS Code Insiders or Windsurf on the computer running your browser**, connected to the DSH server ov
ers or Windsurf on the computer running your browser**, connected to the DSH server over Remote-SSH.
中文文档
## Why
DSH's built-in "Open In..." button launches applications on the machine that runs the DSH server. Th
at works when the browser and the server share a desktop. When you reach DSH from another computer (
a devbox, a VM, a lab server), the button is hidden because the server has no display, and if it wer
e shown, the editor window would open on the server where you cannot see it.
A web page cannot start applications on your computer. It can follow a link whose scheme your operat
ing system hands to an installed app. Cursor and the VS Code family register such schemes, and they
accept Remote-SSH folder links:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
This plugin puts that link on the session header, built from the session's working directory.
## What you get
- A button next to the official "Open In..." control, showing the chosen editor's logo. Clicking it

opens the workspace in your local editor.
- A drop-down panel to choose the editor and the SSH host,

preview the link, and copy it.
- The editor and host are stored in the browser's `localStorage`, be
cause they describe your computer, not the server. Different computers can use different settings ag

ainst the same DSH server.
- The default host is `<server account>@<address in the browser's locatio
n bar>`. Put an `~/.ssh/config` alias there instead when you need a specific key, port or jump host.
- English and Chinese UI, following the DSH language setting.
## Requirements
On the computer running the browser:

- The editor, with its Remote-SSH extension (Cursor and VS Code ship or offer it).
- Working `ssh` a
ccess to the DSH server under the host you configure.
The first time a browser follows a `cursor://` or `vscode://` link it asks whether to open the app;
allow it. If clicking does nothing, the editor is not installed or did not register its URL scheme.
DSH `>=0.2.2-alpha.2 <0.3.0-0` (0.2.x, including its prereleases), Node `>=22.19`.
## Usage
Open any session. Click the button with the editor's logo in the top-right header to open the worksp
ace; click the arrow beside it to change the editor or the SSH host.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The package ships its own bundle patch (`dsh.bundle.patch` + `cordis.patch.yml`), so the CLI and the
Web UI's Plugins page load it in one step. Restart DSH, reload the page and open a session.
## How it works
- **Browser half** (`lib/client.js`): registers one entry in the `conversation.session.header.utilit
ies` slot. It reads the session's `cwd` from the slot's `useSessions` prop, the same source the offi
cial button uses, and renders a plain `<a href="cursor://...">`. A real link keeps the click a user

gesture, so browsers hand the scheme to the OS without navigating the page.
- **Server half** (`lib/
index.js`): one `GET /plugins/remote-editor/api/info` route behind DSH's login check, returning the

server account name for the default host. The server never launches anything.
- Hosts are limited to
letters, digits and `. _ - @ : [ ]`, and each path segment is percent-encoded, so a host or path ca
nnot break out of the link. Paths with `.` or `..` segments and hosts starting with `-` are refused.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`lib/client.js` is committed, because DSH loads it as-is; rebuild it in the same commit as any chang
e under `client/src`.
Bug reports and pull requests are welcome on GitHub. Please include the DSH version, the browser and
OS, and the link shown in the panel.
## License
MIT. Editor logos are from Simple Icons (CC0-1.0); the names and logos are trademarks of their owner
s and are used only to identify the editor that a link opens.
